extract:
Ren, born Ren Gill in 1990, is a Welsh singer, rapper, and multi-instrumentalist who grew up in Brighton, England after being born in Bangor, Wales. He first began performing in the late 2000s, busking on Brighton's streets and playing in the acoustic duo The Big Push with Sam Tompkins around 2010-2012. That early period saw him signed to Sony in his early twenties, but his career was derailed when he became severely ill with what was eventually diagnosed, many years later, as Lyme disease alongside autoimmune complications and psychological struggles. He spent much of the following decade largely offline, battling chronic illness, which became a defining thread in both his personal narrative and his songwriting.

His formative influences span a remarkably wide range — hip hop, folk, blues, singer-songwriter traditions, and theatrical storytelling — and this eclecticism became his signature rather than a liability. Ren is essentially a self-contained artist, writing, producing, and performing his own material, often filming stripped-down performances in his home. After years of dormancy he began uploading music and acoustic videos to YouTube, and the platform, rather than any label push, became the engine of his second act. Tracks like Money Game (and its sequels) gained traction for their rapid-fire verses and pointed critiques of capitalism and mental health, but it was Hi Ren, released in 2022, that transformed his career: a nearly seven-minute dialogue between two sides of himself, alternating between rapped verses and acoustic guitar passages, that went viral and drew millions of viewers into his back catalogue.

On the momentum of Hi Ren, he released the full-length Sick Boi in 2023, an autobiographical record built around his years of illness, followed by the more expansive Sick Boi (Deluxe) and then the 2024 album The Tale of Jenny & Screech, a narrative concept work told across interconnected tracks. He also collaborated with fellow British artist Chinchilla on the single Chalk Outlines in 2023, which became one of his most-streamed songs and reached the UK singles chart. His work has been released independently through his own imprint, The Other Songs having supported some earlier distribution, giving him near-total creative control — a rarity for an artist operating at his scale of audience.

Critical reception has tended to focus on the emotional directness and structural ambition of his songs rather than genre placement, since he moves between rap, folk balladry, spoken word, and rock within single tracks. He has become something of a figurehead for artists who bypass traditional industry gatekeeping, and his transparent discussion of chronic illness, medical gaslighting, and mental health has given him a devoted listener base that treats his releases as events. Fellow independent-minded UK acts and the wider YouTube singer-songwriter ecosystem, including his old collaborator Sam Tompkins, share adjacent territory.

Currently, Ren continues to release music and long-form videos to his growing YouTube following while managing his ongoing health issues, which have at times forced him to cancel touring plans. His legacy, still being written, is already notable as a case study in artistic reinvention outside the major-label system and in the viability of deeply personal, formally ambitious songwriting reaching a mass audience through direct-to-fan channels.
title: Ren
